must_ask.say: Does the pain shoot down past your knee into your foot or toes?
Does coughing, sneezing, or sitting down make the leg pain much worse?
Have you noticed any numbness around your buttocks or loss of bowel or bladder control?
Does raising your straight leg while lying flat trigger the shooting pain?
Do you feel weakness when walking on your heels or toes?

history.answer: My lower back has been hurting for three weeks, and a sharp, burning pain shoots down my right buttock and the back of my thigh.
The pain starts in my right lower back and shoots down through my buttock into the back of my thigh, stopping around my calf.
It started three weeks ago right after I lifted a heavy cooler while packing for a weekend trip.
My back has a dull, deep ache, but down my leg it feels like a sharp, burning electric shock, about a seven out of ten.
Sitting at my desk, bending forward, and coughing or sneezing make the shooting pain much worse. Lying flat with a pillow under my knees gives some relief.
The pain does not wake me up at night, and lying still usually feels much better than sitting or bending.
I feel a little stiff for maybe ten minutes when I get out of bed, but it does not last thirty minutes or improve with walking.
I have tingling and a bit of numbness along the outside of my right calf and the top of my foot.
My right leg feels slightly heavier when I walk, but I haven't noticed my foot catching or tripping.
No, I have normal bladder and bowel control, and no numbness in my groin or saddle area.
Walking does not cause my legs to cramp up, but prolonged sitting definitely triggers the sharp pain down my leg.
No fever, chills, night sweats, or unexplained weight loss at all.
No, I have never had cancer.
No recent infections, no spine injections or back procedures, and I do not use injectable drugs.
No history of osteoporosis, and I have never taken long-term steroids or had any serious falls.
No pain with urination, no blood in my urine, and no abdominal pain or pulsating sensations in my belly.
No eye redness or pain, no heel pain, no chronic diarrhea, and no skin rashes or psoriasis.
I took over-the-counter ibuprofen a couple of times, but it barely took the edge off the pain.
I looked up my symptoms online and I think I might have sciatica or a slipped spinal disc.
I am really worried that this nerve might suffer permanent damage if it is left untreated.
I was hoping to get an MRI scan of my spine and start physical therapy to recover.
I have never had any prior back issues or chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital stays.
I am not taking any regular prescription medications or supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications or food.
I have never smoked cigarettes, and I only have a beer once or twice a month socially.
I work as an office clerk sitting at a computer all day, and I live with my wife.
There is no family history of spine disorders, inflammatory arthritis, or serious medical conditions.

exam.finding: Alert, in mild discomfort when seated; blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 bpm, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Tenderness over the right lower lumbar paraspinal muscles; straight leg raise test on the right produces sharp radiating pain down the posterior thigh at 45 degrees, negative on the left.
Mild weakness on right great toe extension (grade 4/5); normal 5/5 strength in hip flexion, knee extension, knee flexion, and ankle plantarflexion bilaterally.
Decreased sensation to light touch along the right lateral lower leg and dorsal foot; normal light touch sensation in the left lower extremity.
Right Achilles tendon reflex is slightly diminished (1+); patellar reflexes (2+) and left Achilles reflex (2+) are normal, with downward plantar responses bilaterally.
Antalgic gait favoring the right lower limb; able to walk on toes, with mild difficulty walking on the right heel.
Normal anal sphincter tone with intact perianal sensation.
Soft, non-tender abdomen without palpable mass, organomegaly, or abnormal aortic pulsation.
